title: The degree-$g$ part of the Picard scheme is geometrically integral
statement: Let $k$ be a separably closed field and let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over $k$ [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] which is geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], of genus $g=\dim_kH^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$ [def-pc-genus]. Let $\operatorname{Pic}^g_{C/k}$ be the subfunctor of the Picard functor $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ [def-pc-picard-functor] on $(\mathit{Sch}/k)_{fppf}$ consisting of the classes whose fibrewise degree [def-pd-fibrewise-degree] is identically $g$ (equivalently, the fppf sheafification of the subpresheaf $T\mapsto\{\mathcal L\in\operatorname{Pic}(C_T):\deg_T(\mathcal L)(t)=g\text{ for all }t\in T\}$ of the Picard presheaf). Let $P$ be a scheme over $k$ representing $\operatorname{Pic}^g_{C/k}$. Then $P$ is geometrically integral over $k$: for every field extension $k'/k$ the base change $P_{k'}=P\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is an integral scheme.

proof.text: *(1) $P$ is smooth over $k$.* By [prop-pd-picard-degree-decomposition] (2) the open and closed subscheme $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^g_{C/k}$ of the scheme $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}_{C/k}$ representing $\operatorname{Pic}_{C/k}$ represents the subfunctor $\operatorname{Pic}^g_{C/k}$. Since $P$ represents the same functor, there is an isomorphism $P\cong\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^g_{C/k}$ over $k$ [lem-pc-representable-unique]. By the theorem of the base [thm-sc-theorem-of-the-base], $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^g_{C/k}$ is smooth (and proper, of dimension $g$) over $k$; smoothness of the structure morphism [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is invariant under composing with an isomorphism over $k$, so $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth. (The theorem of the base also calls $\underline{\operatorname{Pic}}^g_{C/k}$ a variety, i.e. integral; this is not used: the steps below prove the stronger geometric statement.)

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), clause (1) 'g-dimensional smooth proper varieties' and the proof's third paragraph (smoothness via gamma_g and translates)

proof.text: *(2) $P$ is geometrically reduced.* The structure morphism $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth by step (1), so by [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] it has geometrically reduced fibres. Its only fibre is $P$ itself, over the point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ with residue field $k$; so for every field extension $k'/k$ the base change $P_{k'}=P\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

source.place: Lean docstring of AlgebraicGeometry.geometricallyIntegral_of_representableBy_picardFunctorDegree_genus: 'it is smooth, hence geometrically reduced'; Varieties Tag 056T (smooth over a field implies geometrically reduced)

proof.text: *(3) A surjection from the Hilbert scheme.* $C$ is projective over $k$, hence proper [lem-pc-projective-proper]; it is a curve over $k$ (part of [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve]), smooth over $k$, and geometrically irreducible, being geometrically integral [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. So by [thm-pc-hilb-curves] (1) the functor $\operatorname{Hilb}^g_{C/k}$ is represented by a $k$-scheme $H:=\underline{\operatorname{Hilb}}^g_{C/k}$, and by [lem-sc-hilb-geometrically-integral] (with $X=C$, $d=g$) $H$ is geometrically integral over $k$. With the representing scheme $P$ of $\operatorname{Pic}^g_{C/k}$, [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-morphism] (with $d=g$) gives the $k$-morphism $\gamma_g:H\to P$, $D\mapsto\mathcal O(D)$, defined by the universal divisor, and by [lem-sc-hilb-to-pic-surjective] (with $d=g\geq g$) $\gamma_g$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0BA0 (lemma-picard-pieces), clauses (4), (5) and the proof's second and fourth paragraphs (gamma_d from O(D_univ); gamma_d surjective for d >= g since chi(L) = d+1-g > 0); Tag 0B9I (proposition-hilb-d) (1) and its proof ('in fact geometrically irreducible')

proof.text: *(4) $P$ is geometrically irreducible.* Let $k'/k$ be a field extension and let $\gamma'=\gamma_g\times_k\mathrm{id}:H_{k'}\to P_{k'}$ be the base change of $\gamma_g$. It is the projection $H\times_P P_{k'}\to P_{k'}$ of the fibre product of $\gamma_g$ with the projection $P_{k'}=P\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k'\to P$, because $H\times_P(P\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k')\cong H\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k'=H_{k'}$ (pasting of fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]), compatibly with the maps to $P_{k'}$. Since $\gamma_g$ is surjective (step (3)), $\gamma'$ is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change]. By step (3) $H_{k'}$ is integral, in particular irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme]; the image of the irreducible space $H_{k'}$ under the continuous map underlying $\gamma'$ is irreducible [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-continuous-image], and this image is all of $P_{k'}$. So $P_{k'}$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] (in particular nonempty) for every $k'/k$.

source.place: Tag 0BA0 proof, third and fourth paragraphs (the image of gamma_g is a proper variety; gamma_g surjective), made geometric along the Lean docstring of geometricallyIntegral_of_representableBy_picardFunctorDegree_genus: 'the image of the geometrically integral Hilb^g_{X/k} under D -> O_X(D), so geometrically irreducible'

proof.text: *(5) Conclusion.* For every field extension $k'/k$ the scheme $P_{k'}$ is reduced (step (2)) and irreducible, hence nonempty (step (4)); so it is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Hence $P$ is geometrically integral over $k$ [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].
